*Hint: The eigenvalues of $A$ are $2\pm 5\text{i}.$*

| ${e}^{At}={e}^{2t}\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} | $-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)$ |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

feedback.problem:
Find ${e}^{At}$ for $A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 8 \\ -4 & -3\end{aligned}].$ 

*Hint: The eigenvalues of $A$ are $1\pm 4\text{i}.$*

| ${e}^{At}={e}^{t}\,\,$ |  | $\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)$ | $2\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)$ |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} |  |  |
feedback.worked_solution:
We have a square matrix of dimension $n=2.$ Thus, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{At} & ={\alpha }_{1}At+{\alpha }_{0}I \\  & ={\alpha }_{1}[\begin{aligned}5 & 8 \\ -4 & -3\end{aligned}]t+{\alpha }_{0}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0} & 8{\alpha }_{1}t \\ -4{\alpha }_{1}t & -3{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

where ${\alpha }_{1}$ and ${\alpha }_{0}$ are functions to be determined.

Consider the polynomial $r(\lambda )={\alpha }_{1}\lambda +{\alpha }_{0}.$ The eigenvalues or $At$ are 

$$
{\lambda }_{1}=(1+4\text{i})t,\,{\lambda }_{2}=(1-4\text{i})t,
$$

which are complex conjugates. Thus, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}r((1+4\text{i})t) & ={e}^{(1+4\text{i})t} \\ {\alpha }_{1}(1+4\text{i})t+{\alpha }_{0} & ={e}^{t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)) \\ ({\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0})+4{\alpha }_{1}\text{i}t & ={e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+\text{i}\,{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we equate the real and imaginary parts, and solve for ${\alpha }_{1}$ and ${\alpha }_{0}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0}={e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t) \\ 4t{\alpha }_{1}={e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)\end{aligned}\,⇒\,{\begin{aligned}{\alpha }_{1}=\frac{1}{4t}{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t) \\ {\alpha }_{0}={e}^{t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t))\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${\alpha }_{1}$ and ${\alpha }_{0}$ into the expressions for the required entries of ${e}^{At},$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}5{\alpha }_{1}t+{\alpha }_{0} & =5\cdot \frac{1}{4t}{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)\cdot t+{e}^{t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)) \\  & =\frac{5}{4}{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)+{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)-\frac{1}{4}{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t) \\  & ={e}^{t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)) \\ -4{\alpha }_{1}t & =-4\cdot \frac{1}{4t}{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)\cdot t \\  & =-{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{e}^{At}={e}^{t}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t) & 2\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t) \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)\end{aligned}].
$$
